entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
George IX of Kartli (1525-1534) was the king of the Georgian kingdom of Kartli from 1525 to 1527. He played a crucial role in maintaining relations with neighboring kingdoms and fought against the Ottoman Empire.

The core events during his reign included the Battle of Khevsur, where he defeated the Ottomans, and the establishment of the Church of Christ the Savior in Tbilisi, which became an important center for Georgian Orthodoxy. The king also strengthened ties with Russia, signing a trade agreement that benefited both nations.

Despite these achievements, George IX's reign was cut short due to his death in 1534 from unknown causes. His legacy continued through his successors, who built upon the foundations he established.

In the annals of Georgian history, George IX stands as an emblem of resilience and strategic diplomacy.
